statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-124317: libexpat through 2.10.0 can read past the parse buffer in unknown_toUtf8() and unknown_toUtf16() in xmltok.c when an application registers an unknown encoding and the document ends in a truncated multi-byte sequence (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-124317). Upstream fixed it in libexpat pull request #1492 (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/pull/1492), commits bf26290 and 3d77567 (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/commit/3d77567612994172f9d09b46f31bb604e16fb08d), which check the sequence length against the remaining input before calling the converter. It is released in Expat 2.11.0 (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/blob/R_2_11_0/expat/Changes), and Debian lists only unstable's 2.11.0-1 as fixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-124317). DHI backported both commits to expat 2.10.0 for Alpine 3.23 in build 2.10.0-r2. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes expat builds 2.7.3-r0, 2.7.4-r0, 2.7.5-r0, 2.8.1-r0, 2.8.2-r0, 2.8.3-r0, 2.8.3-r1, 2.8.4-r0, 2.8.5-r0, 2.8.5-r1, 2.9.0-r1, 2.10.0-r1 and 2.10.0-r2. Every build before 2.10.0-r1 was published before the upstream fix was written. We ran the upstream regression test from that pull request (an unknown encoding whose convert callback checks that it is never handed a sequence running past the end of the document) against the libexpat package of 2.10.0-r1 and 2.10.0-r2 on x86_64 and aarch64: with 2.10.0-r1 the callback is called on a sequence that runs past the end of the input, and with 2.10.0-r2 it is not. The request also matches 2.9.0-r0, which the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository does not publish and which sorts below the boundary. The range ends at 2.10.0-r2, the first published build with the fix.

Upstream fixed CVE-2026-124317 (out-of-bounds read in unknown_toUtf8() and unknown_toUtf16() in xmltok.c for application-registered unknown encodings) in libexpat PR #1492, commit 3d77567 (https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/commit/3d77567612994172f9d09b46f31bb604e16fb08d), which makes both converters check the multi-byte sequence length against the remaining input and return XML_CONVERT_INPUT_INCOMPLETE. No Expat release carries it yet and Debian lists it as unfixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-124317). DHI backported that commit to its Debian 13 expat 2.9.0-1~deb13u1 packages from the range's fixed version on. Checked the libexpat1 library with its debug symbols for every 2.9.0 build and the last 2.8.3 build, on amd64 and arm64: in the fixed version and the one later build, unknown_toUtf8() and unknown_toUtf16() are larger than in the earlier builds (amd64 460 and 220 bytes against 421 and 181, arm64 376 and 264 against 348 and 208), matching the added length checks, while other functions such as XmlUtf8Encode() and unknown_isName() are unchanged; the package changelog of those two builds also records the backport. Every earlier published build (upstream 2.7.1, 2.8.2, 2.8.3 and the first two 2.9.0 builds) lacks it and stays on the affected side of the range.
